subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should OpenClaw warn, fail, or stay runtime-only when configured primary, fallback, or per-agent model refs are absent from trusted model catalog evidence?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the correct behavior depends on maintainer intent for custom providers, forward-compatible model names, and whether catalog absence should be advisory or fail-closed.

options.title: Advisory catalog warnings
options.body: Add `config validate` and doctor warnings for catalog-missing configured refs while keeping custom and future refs non-fatal.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject catalog-missing configured refs during validation or config writes, accepting upgrade and custom-provider compatibility risk.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep accepting arbitrary configured refs and rely on improved runtime unknown-model errors plus fallback notices.

recommendation.title: Advisory catalog warnings
recommendation.body: Add `config validate` and doctor warnings for catalog-missing configured refs while keeping custom and future refs non-fatal.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is a model/provider policy choice, and this owner has recent model-selection and doctor-policy history in the affected paths.
